bottom_line: In patients with atrial fibrillation, rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfarin for the prevention of stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
implications: These data support concluding that, in this trial population, rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism in the primary per-protocol analysis (hazard ratio 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority). In the intention-to-treat analysis, superiority over warfarin was not shown (P = 0.12 for superiority). For safety, overall major and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was similar (hazard ratio 1.03; 95% CI, 0.96 to 1.11), while intracranial hemorrhage (0.5% vs. 0.7%, P = 0.02) and fatal bleeding (0.2% vs. 0.5%, P = 0.003) were lower with rivaroxaban.

major_points.text: Multicenter randomized, double-blind, double-dummy trial in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation at increased stroke risk.
major_points.quote: The Rivaroxaban Once Daily Oral Direct Factor Xa Inhibition Compared with Vitamin K Antagonism for Prevention of Stroke and Embolism Trial in Atrial Fibrillation (ROCKET AF) was a multi- center, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy,

major_points.text: Patients were assigned to rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (15 mg daily with creatinine clearance 30–49 ml/min) vs adjusted-dose warfarin (target INR 2.0–3.0).
major_points.quote: Patients were randomly assigned to receive fixed- dose rivaroxaban (20 mg daily or 15 mg daily in patients with a creatinine clearance of 30 to 49 ml per minute) or adjusted-dose warfarin (target in- ternational normalized ratio [INR], 2.0 to 3.0).

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) or systemic embolism; primary analysis was per-protocol while on treatment.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was the compos- ite of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and sys- temic embolism.

major_points.text: In the primary (per-protocol, as-treated) analysis, rivaroxaban reduced stroke/systemic embolism vs warfarin with HR 0.79 (95% CI, 0.66–0.96) and met noninferiority.

guidelines_referenced.text: Seventh ACCP Conference on Antithrombotic and Thrombolytic Therapy
guidelines_referenced.quote: Antithrom- botic therapy in atrial fibrillation: the Seventh ACCP Conference on Antithrom- botic and Thrombolytic Therapy.

inclusion_criteria.text: Nonvalvular atrial fibrillation documented on electrocardiography, at moderate-to-high risk for stroke.
inclusion_criteria.quote: We recruited patients with nonvalvular atrial fibril- lation, as documented on electrocardiography, who were at moderate-to-high risk for stroke.

inclusion_criteria.text: Elevated risk indicated by a history of stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism, or at least two specified risk factors.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Elevated risk was indicated by a history of stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism or at least two of the following risk factors: heart failure or a left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less, hypertension, an age of 75 years or more, or the presence of diabetes mellitus
(i.e., a CHADS2 score of 2 or more, on a scale ranging from 1 to 6, with higher scores indicating a greater risk of stroke).

criticisms.text: Violations in Good Clinical Practice guidelines at one site made the data unreliable and led to exclusion of 93 patients from efficacy analyses.
criticisms.quote: Because of violations in Good Clinical Prac- tice guidelines at one site that made the data un- reliable, 93 patients (50 in the rivaroxaban group and 43 in the warfarin group) were excluded from all efficacy analyses before unblinding.

criticisms.text: Premature, permanent cessation of randomized treatment was slightly higher than in other studies.
criticisms.quote: the rate of premature, permanent cessation of randomized treatment (14.3% in year 1) was slightly higher than in other studies (average, 11%).
